results: 1. smooth pursuit and saccades: ocular motor apraxia - failure to initiate voluntary horizontal saccades with compensatory head thrusts
2. facial dysmorphism and general examination: facial dysmorphism in all patients - broad nasal bridge and low-set ears most common
3. genetic testing (exome): pathogenic variants in ciliopathy genes on exome sequencing
4. MRI brain with DWI: MOLAR TOOTH SIGN with cerebellar vermis hypoplasia and horizontally aligned superior cerebellar peduncles
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Joubert syndrome (Joubert syndrome–related disorder), an autosomal-recessive ciliopathy caused by pathogenic biallelic variants in a Joubert-associated ciliary gene, producing the molar tooth sign, cerebellar vermis hypoplasia, and ocular motor apraxia.
COACH syndrome (cerebellar vermis hypoplasia, oligophrenia, ataxia, coloboma, and hepatic fibrosis)
Orofaciodigital syndrome type VI (Varadi–Papp syndrome)
Poretti–Boltshauser syndrome (LAMA1-related cerebellar dysplasia)
